html:
Fray Bentos is a river town in western Uruguay where a British company began making Liebig's Extract of Meat in 1865. Its factory became one of the largest meat plants in the world and is now a World Heritage Site.

The plains of Uruguay and Argentina held vast herds of cattle, but before refrigeration, beef could not be shipped fresh. The German chemist Justus von Liebig found a way to boil meat into a concentrated extract, and the plant at Fray Bentos turned cattle into extract, and later corned beef, sold across Europe. Its tinned beef fed soldiers in both world wars.

The plant closed in 1979. Its machines, wharves and workers' houses are preserved. Refrigerated ships later brought fresh beef from the region, and meat still drives Uruguay's exports, as it did those of Argentina and the gaucho economy.
